claim_text: Robert Goddard launches the world's first liquid-fueled rocket at Auburn, Massachusetts.
source: Standard histories of rocketry; NASA and Smithsonian historical records
notes: Foundational to spaceflight; 2.5-second flight, ~12.5 m altitude.

claim_text: NBC launches as the first permanent national radio broadcasting network in the US.
notes: RCA-owned; established the national-network model for mass media.

claim_text: Charles Lindbergh completes the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight (New York–Paris) in the Spirit of St. Louis.
source: Smithsonian NASM records; standard aviation histories
notes: Catalyzed public and commercial confidence in aviation.

claim_text: Philo Farnsworth demonstrates the first working all-electronic television image transmission.
notes: First electronic TV image, San Francisco lab, 7 Sep 1927.

claim_text: The Jazz Singer premieres as the first feature-length film with synchronized recorded dialogue, launching the sound-film era.
notes: Ended the silent-film era; Warner Bros./Vitaphone system.

claim_text: Clyde Tombaugh discovers Pluto at Lowell Observatory, the first trans-Neptunian object found.
source: Lowell Observatory records; standard astronomy references
notes: Reclassified as dwarf planet in 2006; unaffected as a discovery milestone.

claim_text: The Empire State Building is completed in New York City, then the tallest building in the world (381 m).
notes: Held world's-tallest title until 1970; built in ~13 months.

claim_text: Ernest Lawrence builds the first working cyclotron at Berkeley, enabling particle acceleration.
notes: First ~11 cm proof-of-concept 1930-31; larger machines followed 1932.

claim_text: The Tennessee Valley Authority is established, a federal authority for regional electrification and river development.
source: US federal statute record; standard New Deal histories
notes: New Deal; both infrastructure and institution — classified by its landmark-institution significance.

claim_text: The Glass–Steagall Banking Act creates federal deposit insurance (FDIC) and separates commercial and investment banking.
source: US federal statute record; standard economic histories
notes: Reshaped US financial regulation for decades; FDIC still operates.

claim_text: The Social Security Act establishes national old-age pensions and unemployment insurance.
source: US federal statute record; Social Security Administration histories
notes: Founding of the modern US social-insurance system.

claim_text: Hoover Dam on the Colorado River is completed, then the world's largest concrete structure and hydroelectric dam.
notes: Construction 1931–1936; dedicated Sep 1935; anchored to 1935 dedication.

claim_text: Wallace Carothers's team at DuPont first synthesizes nylon, the first fully synthetic polymer fiber.
source: Standard histories of materials science; DuPont records
notes: First synthesized 1935; commercial 1938-39; founded the synthetic-fiber industry.

claim_text: The Douglas DC-3 makes its first flight, becoming the airliner that made passenger air travel commercially viable.
source: Smithsonian NASM records; standard aviation histories
notes: First flight Dec 1935; entered service 1936.

claim_text: The Northern Expedition ends with nominal national reunification under the Nationalist (KMT) government seated at Nanjing.
notes: Campaign 1926–1928; anchored to 1928 completion; began the 'Nanjing decade' of partial modernization.

claim_text: Academia Sinica (中央研究院), China's national academy of sciences, is founded at Nanjing.
source: Academia Sinica historical records; standard references
notes: First national modern research-academy institution; both science and durable institution.

claim_text: The Central Bank of China is established in Shanghai as the Nationalist government's central bank.
source: Standard economic histories of Republican China
notes: Part of Nanjing-decade financial-institution building.

claim_text: Pei Wenzhong discovers the first Peking Man (Homo erectus) skullcap at Zhoukoudian.
notes: Major hominin find on Chinese soil by a Chinese scientist; specimens later lost in WWII.

claim_text: The Mass Education Movement's rural-reconstruction experiment at Ding County (Dingxian) scales mass literacy and rural development, led by Y.C. James Yen.
source: Standard histories of Republican-era rural reconstruction
notes: Diffuse program ~1926–1937; anchored ~1929; a landmark in modern Chinese mass-education.

claim_text: The Nanjing-decade government undertakes a national railway, highway, and telecommunications expansion program.
source: Standard economic histories of Republican China
notes: Diffuse buildout ~1928–1937; anchored mid-decade; interrupted by war from 1937. Category populated but low-precision.

claim_text: The fabi (法币) currency reform abandons the silver standard and unifies a managed national paper currency.
source: Standard economic histories of Republican China
notes: Nov 1935; a major monetary-regime shift, though later undermined by wartime inflation.

claim_text: The Chinese Communist Party's Red Army completes the Long March, consolidating Mao Zedong's leadership and the CCP's survival.
source: Standard histories of the Chinese Communist Party
notes: Oct 1934–Oct 1935; primarily a military retreat, admitted for its durable political-institutional consequence, not as a battlefield outcome.

claim_text: Chinese-owned cotton-textile firms (e.g., the Rong family's Shenxin mills) become the leading modern manufacturing sector in the lower Yangtze.
source: Standard economic histories of Republican China
notes: Diffuse; anchored ~1930. Included to populate the industrial category honestly, with low precision noted.

claim_text: The Golden Gate Bridge opens in San Francisco, then the world's longest suspension-bridge main span.
source: US National Park Service records; standard engineering references
notes: 1,280 m main span; iconic Depression-era public works.

claim_text: Chester Carlson produces the first xerographic image, inventing electrophotography (later Xerox copying).
source: Standard histories of technology; US patent record
notes: Founded the office-copying industry; commercialized by Haloid/Xerox in the 1950s-60s.

claim_text: Hewlett-Packard is founded in Palo Alto, an origin point of what became Silicon Valley.
notes: First product an audio oscillator; archetypal garage startup.

claim_text: Enrico Fermi's team achieves the first controlled, self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction (Chicago Pile-1).
source: Standard physics histories; US Manhattan Project records
notes: Dec 2, 1942; foundational to both nuclear power and weapons.

claim_text: Grand Coulee Dam on the Columbia River is completed, the largest concrete structure and hydroelectric plant in the US.
notes: Main dam completed 1942; first power 1941; anchored to 1942 completion.

claim_text: US pharmaceutical firms achieve deep-tank fermentation mass production of penicillin, enabling the first antibiotic at scale.
source: Standard histories of medicine; USDA Peoria lab records
notes: Scale-up 1943-1944; transformed infection treatment; discovery itself was British (Fleming/Florey/Chain).

claim_text: US wartime industrial mobilization mass-produces ships and aircraft at unprecedented scale (Liberty ships, tens of thousands of aircraft).
source: Standard economic/WWII histories; US wartime production records
notes: ~1941–1945; ~2,700 Liberty ships; the 'Arsenal of Democracy'; anchored to 1943 peak.

claim_text: The Bretton Woods conference establishes the IMF and the framework for the World Bank, anchoring the postwar monetary order.
source: IMF/World Bank founding records; standard economic histories
notes: July 1944; US-led postwar financial architecture and the dollar's central role.

claim_text: The GI Bill (Servicemen's Readjustment Act) funds mass higher education and home ownership for returning veterans.
source: US federal statute record; standard social histories
notes: Widely credited with expanding the postwar middle class and university system.

claim_text: ENIAC, the first general-purpose electronic digital computer, becomes operational.
source: Standard computing histories; US Army records
notes: Built 1943-1945; operational late 1945; publicly unveiled Feb 1946; anchored to 1945.

claim_text: The Manhattan Project achieves the first nuclear detonation (Trinity test), demonstrating engineered nuclear fission at scale.
source: US Manhattan Project records; standard histories
notes: July 16, 1945; recorded as a science/industrial milestone; military application to Hiroshima/Nagasaki noted, not the ledger's frame.

claim_text: Vannevar Bush's report 'Science, the Endless Frontier' sets the blueprint for federal funding of basic research (leading to the NSF).
source: US government report record; standard science-policy histories
notes: July 1945; foundational to the postwar US research-university-government compact.

claim_text: The Qiantang River Bridge at Hangzhou, chief-engineered by Mao Yisheng, opens as the first modern double-deck road-and-rail bridge designed and built by Chinese engineers.
notes: Opened Sept 1937; deliberately demolished Dec 1937 to slow the Japanese advance, then rebuilt postwar.

claim_text: The National Southwestern Associated University (Xinan Lianda) forms in Kunming, merging Peking, Tsinghua, and Nankai universities to preserve higher education through the war.
source: Standard histories of modern Chinese education
notes: 1938-1946; alumni include future Nobel physicists; a landmark in intellectual resilience.

claim_text: The Chinese Industrial Cooperatives ('Gung Ho') movement organizes decentralized wartime production across the interior.
notes: Founded 1938; sustained small-scale industry away from occupied coasts.

claim_text: China relocates key industries and universities to the southwestern interior (Chongqing, Sichuan) to sustain wartime production and scholarship.
source: Standard economic histories of wartime China
notes: Diffuse ~1937–1940; one of the era's largest wartime industrial migrations; anchored ~1940.

claim_text: The US and UK relinquish extraterritorial rights in China by treaty, ending a century of the 'unequal treaties'.
notes: Jan 1943; a major sovereignty milestone for the Republic of China.

claim_text: China becomes a founding member of the United Nations and a permanent member of the Security Council.
notes: UN Charter signed June 1945 (Republic of China); recognized China's great-power status.

claim_text: Bell Labs invents the point-contact transistor (Bardeen, Brattain, Shockley), foundation of all modern electronics.
notes: Dec 1947; arguably the century's most consequential device.

claim_text: Chuck Yeager pilots the Bell X-1 to the first crewed supersonic flight, breaking the sound barrier.
source: US Air Force / NACA records; standard aviation histories
notes: Oct 14, 1947; opened the supersonic era.

claim_text: The Marshall Plan (European Recovery Program) begins large-scale US-funded reconstruction of Western Europe.
source: US federal statute record; standard economic histories
notes: Enacted 1948; ~$13bn; anchored US postwar economic leadership.

claim_text: Claude Shannon publishes 'A Mathematical Theory of Communication', founding information theory.
source: Bell System Technical Journal (1948); standard references
notes: Defined the bit; underlies all digital communication and computing.

claim_text: The US leads the founding of NATO, the postwar transatlantic security institution.
notes: April 1949; durable alliance institution centered on US power.

claim_text: UNIVAC I is delivered as the first commercially produced electronic computer in the US.
notes: First delivered to the US Census Bureau; began the commercial computer industry.

claim_text: The US detonates 'Ivy Mike', the first full-scale thermonuclear (hydrogen) device.
source: US Atomic Energy Commission records; standard histories
notes: Nov 1952; recorded as a thermonuclear-science milestone; weapons context noted.

claim_text: The NTSC color television standard is adopted, launching compatible color broadcasting in the US.
notes: RCA-led compatible color system; consumer color TV followed through the 1950s-60s.

claim_text: USS Nautilus is commissioned as the world's first nuclear-powered submarine.
notes: Untethered submerged endurance transformed naval power and reactor engineering.

claim_text: Bell Labs demonstrates the first practical silicon solar cell.
source: Standard histories of photovoltaics; Bell Labs records
notes: ~6% efficiency; ancestor of modern photovoltaics.

claim_text: Levittown, New York begins mass-produced suburban housing, a template for postwar American suburbanization.
notes: Assembly-line homebuilding; reshaped US settlement patterns (and its exclusionary covenants are part of the record).

claim_text: Jonas Salk's inactivated polio vaccine is licensed after mass field trials, curbing a feared epidemic disease.
source: US Public Health Service records; standard medical histories
notes: Field trials 1954; licensed 1955; anchored to licensing.

claim_text: Ray Kroc launches the McDonald's franchise system, a template for standardized mass-service industry.
notes: Scaled the franchise operating model that reshaped global consumer services.

claim_text: The People's Republic of China is founded, ending decades of civil war and fragmentation on the mainland.
notes: Oct 1, 1949; the defining political event of modern China; ROC government relocates to Taiwan.

claim_text: The Marriage Law of 1950 bans arranged and child marriage and establishes new legal rights for women.
source: PRC statute record; standard social histories
notes: One of the PRC's first major social reforms.

claim_text: Nationwide Land Reform redistributes land from landlords to peasants under the 1950 Agrarian Reform Law.
notes: ~1950–1953; vast social restructuring; accompanied by violent class struggle, part of the record.

claim_text: The new government halts hyperinflation and stabilizes the renminbi, restoring monetary order.
source: Standard economic histories of the early PRC
notes: Chen Yun's 1950 stabilization measures ended years of runaway inflation.

claim_text: The Chengdu–Chongqing (Chengyu) Railway opens, the first railway wholly built by the PRC.
notes: Completed July 1952; symbol of early PRC construction capacity.

claim_text: Industrial and agricultural output recovers to pre-1937 peak levels three years after founding.
source: Standard economic histories of the PRC
notes: Anchored ~1952; a widely-cited recovery benchmark, though early-PRC statistics carry reliability caveats.

claim_text: The Patriotic Health Campaign mobilizes mass sanitation and disease-control drives nationwide.
source: Standard public-health histories of the PRC
notes: Launched 1952; early foundation of large gains in basic public health.

claim_text: The First Five-Year Plan begins Soviet-aided heavy industrialization built around 156 key projects.
source: PRC planning records; standard economic histories
notes: 1953–1957; laid China's initial modern industrial base; anchored to 1953 start.

claim_text: China conducts its first modern national census, counting roughly 583 million people.
notes: 1953; a major state-capacity milestone (and a contested figure in some later analyses).

claim_text: The first Constitution of the PRC is adopted and the first National People's Congress convenes.
notes: Sept 1954; formalized the new state's governing framework.

claim_text: Qian Xuesen returns from the US to China, seeding the country's missile and later space programs.
source: Standard histories of Chinese science and the space program
notes: Oct 1955; a foundational figure for the 'Two Bombs, One Satellite' program.

claim_text: The Federal-Aid Highway Act launches the Interstate Highway System, the largest US public-works program.
source: US federal statute record; standard references
notes: ~48,000 miles; reshaped US commerce, mobility, and suburbanization.

claim_text: IBM ships the RAMAC 305, the first computer with a moving-head hard disk drive.
notes: Invented random-access magnetic disk storage.

claim_text: NASA is established as the US civilian space agency.
notes: Response to Sputnik; institutionalized the US space effort.

claim_text: Explorer 1, the first US satellite, reaches orbit and discovers the Van Allen radiation belts.
notes: Jan 1958; first US space science result.

claim_text: Jack Kilby at Texas Instruments demonstrates the first integrated circuit.
notes: Robert Noyce's parallel silicon IC (1959) followed; together they founded microelectronics.

claim_text: Theodore Maiman operates the first working laser.
source: Standard physics histories; Hughes Research Labs records
notes: May 1960; enabled fiber optics, medicine, manufacturing, and consumer electronics.

claim_text: The FDA approves the first oral contraceptive pill.
source: US FDA records; standard social histories
notes: Reshaped family planning, women's workforce participation, and demography.

claim_text: Alan Shepard becomes the first American in space aboard a Mercury capsule.
notes: May 1961; preceded by Gagarin (USSR); catalyzed the Apollo commitment.

claim_text: Telstar 1, the first active communications satellite, relays the first live transatlantic television.
notes: Began the satellite-communications era.

claim_text: IBM introduces the System/360, the first compatible family of mainframe computers.
notes: Standardized enterprise computing; a landmark industrial bet.

claim_text: The Civil Rights Act of 1964 outlaws discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, or national origin.
notes: Landmark of the civil-rights era.

claim_text: The Voting Rights Act of 1965 bans racial discrimination in voting.
notes: Enforced the 15th Amendment; transformed political participation.

claim_text: Medicare and Medicaid are created, establishing federal health coverage for the elderly and poor.
notes: Largest expansion of the US social-insurance state since 1935.

claim_text: The First Automobile Works produces the Jiefang CA-10 truck, the first motor vehicle manufactured in China.
notes: July 1956; start of an indigenous auto industry; first domestic cars (Dongfeng/Hongqi) followed 1958.

claim_text: The 'socialist transformation' of industry and commerce is completed, converting private enterprise to public/joint ownership.
source: Standard economic histories of the PRC
notes: Nationalized the urban economy within a few years of founding.

claim_text: The Wuhan Yangtze River Bridge opens, the first bridge to span the Yangtze, carrying rail and road.
notes: Oct 1957; linked north-south rail; a signature early-PRC engineering feat (with Soviet assistance).

claim_text: Hanyu Pinyin romanization is adopted, complementing simplified characters in a national literacy drive.
notes: Simplified-character scheme 1956; Pinyin 1958; tools behind large literacy gains.

claim_text: The Daqing oilfield is discovered, launching China's path to petroleum self-sufficiency.
notes: Discovered 1959; by ~1963 China was largely oil self-sufficient; 'Iron Man' Wang Jinxi became a national symbol.

claim_text: The Great Hall of the People and the 'Ten Great Buildings' are completed for the PRC's tenth anniversary.
source: Standard architectural histories of the PRC
notes: Rapid monumental construction in Beijing, 1958-1959.

claim_text: China detonates its first atomic bomb, becoming the fifth nuclear-weapons state.
source: Standard histories of the Chinese nuclear program
notes: Oct 16, 1964 (Project 596); recorded as a science/engineering milestone of the 'Two Bombs, One Satellite' program.

claim_text: The 'Third Front' program begins building a dispersed heavy-industrial base in China's interior.
source: Standard economic histories of the PRC
notes: From 1964; a massive, costly inland industrialization; diffuse, anchored to 1964 start.

claim_text: Chinese scientists achieve the first total synthesis of crystalline bovine insulin, the first synthesis of a functional protein.
source: Standard histories of biochemistry; contemporaneous reports
notes: Sept 1965, Shanghai; a genuine world scientific first, often under-credited in English-language sources.

claim_text: Apollo 11 lands the first humans on the Moon.
notes: July 20, 1969; the culmination of the Space Race.

claim_text: ARPANET carries its first host-to-host message, the direct ancestor of the internet.
notes: Oct 1969; packet-switched networking.

claim_text: Bell Labs develops the Unix operating system.
source: Standard computing histories; Bell Labs records
notes: With C (1972), the basis of most modern operating systems.

claim_text: The Boeing 747 enters commercial service, inaugurating the wide-body jumbo-jet era.
notes: Democratized long-haul air travel for decades.

claim_text: The Environmental Protection Agency is created and the Clean Air Act is strengthened.
notes: Founded modern US environmental regulation.

claim_text: Intel ships the 4004, the first commercially available microprocessor.
notes: Put a general-purpose CPU on a single chip.

claim_text: The US ends dollar-gold convertibility (the 'Nixon shock'), collapsing the Bretton Woods fixed-rate system.
source: US federal records; standard economic histories
notes: Aug 1971; ushered in the era of floating fiat currencies.

claim_text: NASDAQ launches as the first electronic stock market.
notes: Screen-based trading that later hosted the tech-company boom.

claim_text: Pioneer 10 launches, becoming the first spacecraft to traverse the asteroid belt and fly by Jupiter.
notes: First mission to the outer solar system.

claim_text: Cohen and Boyer demonstrate practical recombinant DNA, founding genetic engineering and biotechnology.
notes: Enabled the biotech industry (Genentech founded 1976).

claim_text: Robert Metcalfe invents Ethernet at Xerox PARC.
source: Standard computing histories; Xerox PARC records
notes: The dominant local-area-networking standard.

claim_text: Motorola's Martin Cooper places the first handheld cellular phone call.
notes: April 1973; prototype of the mobile-phone era.

claim_text: The Altair 8800 sparks the personal-computer movement and Microsoft is founded.
notes: 1975; hobbyist PCs and the software industry take off.

claim_text: China detonates its first hydrogen bomb, only 32 months after its first atomic test.
source: Standard histories of the Chinese nuclear program
notes: June 1967; an unusually fast A-to-H progression.

claim_text: The Nanjing Yangtze River Bridge opens, the first Yangtze bridge designed and built entirely by China.
notes: Dec 1968; a self-reliance milestone after Soviet withdrawal, unlike the Soviet-aided Wuhan bridge.

claim_text: The 'barefoot doctors' program scales basic rural healthcare to hundreds of millions.
notes: From ~1968; credited in large gains in rural life expectancy; praised by the WHO.

claim_text: China launches its first satellite, Dong Fang Hong 1, becoming the fifth nation to reach orbit.
source: Standard histories of the Chinese space program
notes: April 1970; completed the 'Two Bombs, One Satellite' program.

claim_text: The PRC takes China's United Nations seat, including permanent Security Council membership.
notes: Oct 1971; replaced the ROC; a decisive return to the world stage.

claim_text: Tu Youyou's team isolates artemisinin (qinghaosu), a highly effective antimalarial, under Project 523.
source: Standard histories of medicine; Nobel records (2015)
notes: ~1972; later a global malaria treatment; Nobel Prize 2015; developed during the Cultural Revolution.

claim_text: President Nixon's visit and the Shanghai Communiqué begin US-China rapprochement.
notes: Feb 1972; reopened China's ties with the West, preceding reform and opening.

claim_text: Yuan Longping's team achieves the first high-yield hybrid rice, a major advance for food security.
notes: First successful three-line hybrid ~1973; large-scale deployment followed; credited with feeding tens of millions.

claim_text: The Terracotta Army is discovered near Xi'an, one of the century's great archaeological finds.
notes: March 1974; Qin Shi Huang's mausoleum complex.

claim_text: China launches and recovers its first returnable satellite, the third nation to achieve satellite recovery.
source: Standard histories of the Chinese space program
notes: Nov 1975; a key step toward reconnaissance and later crewed spaceflight.

claim_text: Apple is founded and the Apple II (1977) helps launch the personal-computer industry.
notes: Anchored to 1976 founding; Apple II shipped 1977.

claim_text: Seymour Cray's Cray-1 defines the modern supercomputer.
notes: Vector supercomputing; ~160 MFLOPS.

claim_text: NASA launches Voyager 1 and 2 on a grand tour of the outer planets.
notes: Both later crossed into interstellar space; still returning data decades on.

claim_text: The Atari 2600 popularizes the cartridge-based home video-game console.
source: Standard histories of the video-game industry
notes: Seeded a major entertainment industry.

claim_text: The first GPS (Navstar) satellite is launched, beginning the global positioning system.
notes: Full constellation reached the 1990s; now core global infrastructure.

claim_text: The Bayh-Dole Act and Genentech's IPO catalyze university tech-transfer and the biotechnology industry.
source: US federal statute record; standard business histories
notes: Aligned university research with commercialization; biotech becomes an industry.

claim_text: IBM introduces the IBM PC, standardizing the personal-computer platform.
notes: The open architecture created a vast hardware/software ecosystem.

claim_text: The Space Shuttle Columbia makes the first flight of a reusable crewed spacecraft.
notes: April 1981; reusable orbiter concept.

claim_text: Surgeons implant the Jarvik-7, the first permanent artificial heart in a human.
notes: 1982; advanced mechanical circulatory support.

claim_text: ARPANET switches to TCP/IP, the moment usually called the birth of the internet.
notes: Jan 1, 1983; the protocol suite that unified networks.

claim_text: Apple's Macintosh brings the graphical user interface and mouse to a mass consumer market.
notes: 1984; popularized the GUI paradigm.

claim_text: Microsoft releases Windows 1.0, beginning its dominant PC graphical operating environment.
notes: 1985; Windows later became the dominant desktop OS.

claim_text: The Cultural Revolution ends with Mao Zedong's death and the arrest of the Gang of Four.
notes: 1976; cleared the way for the reform era.

claim_text: The national college entrance examination (gaokao) is restored and universities reopen.
notes: Dec 1977; reopened higher education after a decade of disruption; a human-capital turning point.

claim_text: Reform and Opening is launched at the Third Plenum, beginning China's market-oriented transformation.
source: Standard economic histories of the PRC
notes: Dec 1978; Deng Xiaoping era; arguably the most consequential policy shift of the century for China.

claim_text: The Household Responsibility System decollectivizes agriculture, sharply raising farm output and rural incomes.
source: Standard economic histories of the PRC
notes: From Xiaogang village, 1978; spread nationwide by the early 1980s.

claim_text: The US and China establish full diplomatic relations.
notes: Jan 1, 1979; integral to opening China's economy to global trade and investment.

claim_text: China establishes its first Special Economic Zones, with Shenzhen as the flagship.
source: PRC policy records; standard economic histories
notes: 1980; Shenzhen grew from a small town to a megacity, a model for export-led development.

claim_text: China joins the IMF and the World Bank, rejoining the core global economic institutions.
notes: 1980; reintegrated China into the multilateral financial system.

claim_text: China introduces the one-child policy, a sweeping state intervention in fertility.
source: PRC policy records; standard demographic histories
notes: Formalized 1980; curbed population growth but drove later aging and sex-ratio problems (part of the record).

claim_text: China completes Yinhe-I (Galaxy-1), its first domestically built supercomputer.
notes: 1983; ~100 MFLOPS; built at the National University of Defense Technology.

claim_text: Lenovo (Legend) and Haier are founded, among the first globally competitive Chinese technology and consumer firms.
notes: 1984; early markers of Chinese commercial innovation emerging from the reform economy.

claim_text: China opens fourteen coastal cities to foreign investment, widening the reform beyond the SEZs.
source: PRC policy records; standard economic histories
notes: 1984; extended the export-oriented coastal development model.

claim_text: China establishes Great Wall Station, its first Antarctic research base.
source: Standard histories of Chinese polar science
notes: Feb 1985; entry into polar research.

claim_text: NSFNET establishes a national backbone that scales the internet toward public use.
notes: 1986; bridged ARPANET-era research networks to the mass internet.

claim_text: TAT-8, the first transatlantic fiber-optic telecommunications cable, enters service.
notes: Vastly increased intercontinental bandwidth.

claim_text: The Hubble Space Telescope is launched, transforming observational astronomy.
notes: 1990; deep-field imaging reshaped cosmology (US-led with ESA).

claim_text: The Human Genome Project begins, the US-led international effort to sequence human DNA.
notes: 1990-2003; foundational to genomics and modern biomedicine.

claim_text: The NCSA Mosaic browser makes the World Wide Web usable and ignites its explosive growth.
notes: 1993; the Web itself was invented at CERN (Europe); Mosaic drove mass adoption.

claim_text: Intel launches the Pentium processor.
notes: Defined mainstream PC performance through the 1990s.

claim_text: Netscape and Amazon are founded, launching the commercial web and e-commerce.
notes: 1994; the browser war and online retail begin.

claim_text: NAFTA takes effect, creating a continental free-trade area.
source: US federal records; standard economic histories
notes: Jan 1994; deep North American economic integration.

claim_text: Microsoft releases Windows 95, bringing modern GUI computing to the mass market.
notes: 1995; blockbuster consumer OS launch.

claim_text: Sun releases Java, a write-once-run-anywhere programming platform for the networked era.
notes: Became a dominant enterprise and, later, mobile platform.

claim_text: GPS reaches full operational capability, providing global positioning as public infrastructure.
notes: 1995; underpins navigation, logistics, finance, and telecom timing.

claim_text: eBay is founded, pioneering large-scale online marketplaces.
notes: 1995; consumer-to-consumer e-commerce at scale.

claim_text: China launches the '863 Program', a national high-technology R&D initiative.
source: PRC policy records; standard S&T histories
notes: March 1986; steered state investment into biotech, IT, space, lasers, and automation.

claim_text: The Beijing Electron-Positron Collider begins operation, China's first major high-energy physics facility.
notes: 1988; entry into frontier particle physics.

claim_text: Hainan becomes a province and China's largest Special Economic Zone.
notes: 1988; extended the SEZ experiment to a whole island province.

claim_text: The Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges open, restoring equity markets in China.
notes: 1990; capital markets return four decades after 1949.

claim_text: China launches development of the Pudong New Area, transforming Shanghai into a global financial hub.
source: PRC policy records; standard economic histories
notes: April 1990; farmland to skyline within two decades.

claim_text: China hosts the Beijing Asian Games, its first large international multi-sport event.
notes: Sept 1990; a coming-out event and infrastructure push, prefiguring the 2008 Olympics.

claim_text: The Qinshan Nuclear Power Plant, China's first domestically designed nuclear station, connects to the grid.
source: Standard histories of Chinese nuclear power
notes: Dec 1991; indigenous civilian nuclear power begins.

claim_text: Deng Xiaoping's Southern Tour reaccelerates reform; the '14th Party Congress' adopts the 'socialist market economy'.
source: Standard economic histories of the PRC
notes: 1992; ended post-1989 stagnation and locked in market reform.

claim_text: China enacts tax-sharing fiscal reform and unifies its exchange rate, foundations of its high-growth era.
source: Standard economic histories of the PRC
notes: 1994; rebuilt central fiscal capacity and made exports more competitive.

claim_text: China establishes full internet connectivity with a first TCP/IP link to the global network.
source: Standard histories of the Chinese internet
notes: April 1994; the on-ramp for China's later internet economy (first email had been sent in 1987).

claim_text: Rapid reform-era growth lifts hundreds of millions of Chinese above the poverty line.
source: World Bank poverty and development indicators
notes: Diffuse ~1981 onward; anchored ~1990; one of the largest poverty reductions in recorded history (a bedrock, if partly definition-dependent, achievement).

claim_text: IBM's Deep Blue defeats world chess champion Garry Kasparov, a landmark for machine intelligence.
notes: May 1997; first computer to beat a reigning world champion under tournament conditions.

claim_text: Mars Pathfinder lands and deploys Sojourner, the first successful Mars rover.
notes: 1997; pioneered mobile robotic exploration of Mars.

claim_text: Google is founded, reorganizing access to the world's information around search.
notes: 1998; became the dominant search and online-advertising company.

claim_text: Assembly of the International Space Station begins, the largest crewed structure in orbit.
notes: 1998; US-led multinational orbital laboratory.

claim_text: Wikipedia launches, creating the largest collaborative reference work in history.
notes: 2001; open, crowd-edited knowledge at global scale.

claim_text: Apple releases the iPod, reshaping digital music and consumer devices.
notes: 2001; presaged the smartphone-era device business.

claim_text: SpaceX is founded, catalyzing low-cost, reusable commercial spaceflight.
notes: 2002; later achieved orbital rocket reuse (2015-onward).

claim_text: The Human Genome Project is completed, delivering an essentially finished human reference genome.
notes: April 2003; foundational reference for biomedicine.

claim_text: Tesla is founded, helping launch the modern electric-vehicle industry.
notes: 2003; mass-market EVs followed (Model S, 2012).

claim_text: Facebook is founded, launching the era of mass social networking.
notes: 2004; reshaped media, advertising, and social interaction.

claim_text: NASA lands the Spirit and Opportunity rovers on Mars for long-duration exploration.
notes: 2004; Opportunity operated for ~15 years.

claim_text: YouTube is founded, creating mass online video and the creator economy.
notes: 2005; user-generated video at global scale.

claim_text: Hong Kong (1997) and Macau (1999) return to Chinese sovereignty under 'one country, two systems'.
notes: Anchored to 1997; closed the last colonial-era territorial questions on the coast.

claim_text: China's national expressway network expands explosively, becoming among the world's largest.
notes: Accelerated after the 1998 stimulus; ~41,000 km by 2005; anchored to 1998.

claim_text: Tencent (1998), Alibaba (1999), and Baidu (2000) are founded, the core of China's internet economy.
notes: Anchored to 1999; grew into some of the world's largest technology firms.

claim_text: China launches the Western Development Strategy to industrialize and connect its interior.
notes: 2000; major long-run infrastructure and investment program for inland provinces.

claim_text: China accedes to the World Trade Organization, integrating into the global trading system.
notes: Dec 2001; arguably the single biggest accelerant of China's export-led rise.

claim_text: China becomes the world's largest mobile-phone market by subscribers.
notes: ~2001; surpassed the US; presaged its mobile-internet leadership.

claim_text: China becomes the world's largest recipient of foreign direct investment.
notes: 2002; signaled its emergence as the global manufacturing base.

claim_text: Shenzhou 5 carries Yang Liwei to orbit, China's first crewed spaceflight.
source: Standard histories of the Chinese space program
notes: Oct 2003; third country to independently launch a human into space.

claim_text: China completes its ~1% share of the Human Genome Project, the only developing country in the consortium.
notes: 2003; sequenced part of chromosome 3; entry into frontier genomics (via BGI).

claim_text: China consolidates its position as the 'workshop of the world' across many manufactured goods.
notes: Early 2000s; diffuse; anchored ~2003; leadership in an expanding set of product categories.

claim_text: Lenovo acquires IBM's personal-computer division, an emblematic Chinese firm going global.
notes: Completed 2005; made Lenovo a top-tier global PC maker.

claim_text: Amazon Web Services launches, creating the modern cloud-computing industry.
notes: 2006; utility computing that underpins much of the modern internet.

claim_text: Apple releases the iPhone, defining the modern smartphone.
notes: 2007; reorganized computing, media, and communications around the pocket device.

claim_text: SpaceX's Falcon 1 becomes the first privately developed liquid-fueled rocket to reach orbit.
notes: Sept 2008; opened the private-orbital-launch era.

claim_text: Apple's App Store launches, creating the mobile-application economy.
notes: 2008; a vast new software distribution and developer economy.

claim_text: Craig Venter's team builds the first cell controlled by a synthetic genome.
source: Standard histories of biology; J. Craig Venter Institute
notes: 2010; a milestone in synthetic biology.

claim_text: The Affordable Care Act expands US health-insurance coverage.
notes: 2010; the largest health-coverage expansion since Medicare/Medicaid.

claim_text: IBM's Watson defeats champions at Jeopardy!, showcasing natural-language AI.
notes: 2011; a public marker of machine language understanding.

claim_text: NASA lands the Curiosity rover on Mars for long-duration science.
notes: 2012; sky-crane landing of a car-sized nuclear-powered rover.

claim_text: Doudna and Charpentier demonstrate programmable CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing.
source: Standard histories of molecular biology; Nobel records (2020)
notes: 2012; US-France collaboration; transformed genetics and medicine.

claim_text: The shale revolution makes the US the world's largest producer of oil and natural gas.
notes: ~2013-2014; hydraulic fracturing and horizontal drilling reshaped global energy.

claim_text: SpaceX lands an orbital rocket's first stage, proving reusable launch vehicles.
notes: Dec 2015; drove launch costs down sharply in the following years.

claim_text: LIGO makes the first direct detection of gravitational waves.
notes: Detected Sept 2015 (announced 2016); confirmed a century-old prediction and opened a new astronomy.

claim_text: The US Supreme Court establishes a nationwide right to same-sex marriage (Obergefell).
notes: 2015; a landmark civil-rights ruling.

claim_text: The Qinghai-Tibet Railway opens, the highest railway in the world.
notes: 2006; engineering across permafrost above 5,000 m connecting Tibet to the national network.

claim_text: The Three Gorges Dam is completed as the world's largest hydroelectric power station.
notes: Dam structure completed 2006; final generating unit 2012; ~22.5 GW; large displacement and ecological costs are part of the record.

claim_text: China launches Chang'e 1, its first lunar orbiter.
source: Standard histories of the Chinese space program
notes: 2007; start of a sustained lunar-exploration program.

claim_text: China hosts the Beijing Summer Olympics, a landmark of national arrival and infrastructure.
notes: Aug 2008; accompanied by major transport and urban construction.

claim_text: The Beijing-Tianjin intercity line opens, launching China's high-speed rail network.
notes: Aug 2008; first 350 km/h service; seed of the world's largest HSR system.

claim_text: Shenzhou 7 conducts China's first spacewalk.
source: Standard histories of the Chinese space program
notes: Sept 2008; Zhai Zhigang's EVA.

claim_text: China becomes the world's second-largest economy, surpassing Japan.
notes: 2010; nominal GDP; a symbolic threshold in the US-China comparison.

claim_text: China becomes the world's largest manufacturing nation and merchandise exporter.
notes: ~2009-2010; overtook the US in manufacturing value added; exporter #1 from 2009.

claim_text: Chang'e 3 and the Yutu rover achieve China's first soft landing on the Moon.
source: Standard histories of the Chinese space program
notes: Dec 2013; first lunar soft landing by any nation since 1976.

claim_text: Tianhe-2 becomes the world's fastest supercomputer.
notes: Ranked #1 from 2013 to 2015; a marker of China's high-performance-computing rise.

claim_text: China's high-speed rail network becomes the world's largest, exceeding the rest of the world combined.
notes: ~16,000 km by 2014; the signature Chinese infrastructure achievement of the era.

claim_text: Alibaba's IPO becomes the largest in history to that point, marking China's internet economy on the world stage.
notes: Sept 2014, NYSE, ~$25bn.

claim_text: Mobile payments (Alipay, WeChat Pay) leapfrog cards to make China a world leader in cashless transactions.
notes: ~2014-2015; diffuse; anchored 2014; QR-code payments become near-universal.

claim_text: Tu Youyou wins the Nobel Prize in Medicine for artemisinin, China's first science Nobel for work done in China.
notes: Oct 2015; recognition for the 1970s Project 523 antimalarial work.

claim_text: Google researchers publish the Transformer architecture ('Attention Is All You Need'), the basis of modern large language models.
notes: 2017; underlies the generative-AI boom of the 2020s.

claim_text: SpaceX flies the Falcon Heavy, the most powerful operational rocket of its time, with reusable boosters.
notes: 2018; demonstrated heavy-lift with booster recovery.

claim_text: SpaceX begins deploying Starlink, the first large low-Earth-orbit satellite-internet constellation.
notes: From 2020; thousands of satellites providing global broadband.

claim_text: SpaceX Crew Dragon flies the first commercial crewed orbital mission, restoring US human launch capability.
notes: May 2020; first crewed orbital flight from US soil since 2011.

claim_text: The first mRNA vaccines (COVID-19) are developed and authorized at record speed.
source: US FDA records; standard medical literature
notes: Dec 2020; Moderna (US) and Pfizer-BioNTech (US-Germany); a new vaccine platform at scale.

claim_text: NASA's Ingenuity performs the first powered, controlled flight on another planet.
notes: April 2021; first aircraft to fly on Mars.

claim_text: The James Webb Space Telescope returns its first images, the most powerful space observatory ever.
notes: July 2022; US-led with European and Canadian partners.

claim_text: The National Ignition Facility achieves fusion ignition with net energy gain from the reaction.
source: US Department of Energy / LLNL records
notes: Dec 2022; first laboratory fusion shot to yield more energy than the laser delivered to the target.

claim_text: The CHIPS and Science Act commits large federal funding to reshore semiconductor manufacturing and research.
notes: 2022; industrial policy aimed at the semiconductor supply chain.

claim_text: The Inflation Reduction Act enacts the largest US federal investment in clean energy and climate.
notes: 2022; ~$370bn in energy and climate provisions.

claim_text: OpenAI releases ChatGPT, triggering mass adoption of generative AI.
notes: Nov 2022; fastest-growing consumer application of its time; GPT-4 followed 2023.

claim_text: SpaceX catches a returning Starship booster with its launch tower, a step toward rapid full reuse.
notes: 2024; 'chopsticks' catch of the Super Heavy booster.

claim_text: Nvidia's AI accelerators drive it to briefly become the world's most valuable company, marking US dominance in AI hardware.
notes: 2024; the AI-compute build-out; US firms lead advanced AI chips and models.

claim_text: China launches Micius, the world's first quantum-communications satellite.
notes: Aug 2016; demonstrated satellite-based quantum key distribution and entanglement, a world first.

claim_text: China completes FAST, the world's largest single-dish radio telescope.
notes: 2016; 500 m aperture; a frontier astronomy instrument.

claim_text: China's C919, its first domestically developed large passenger jet, makes its maiden flight.
notes: May 2017; entered commercial service 2023; challenges the Airbus/Boeing duopoly (with foreign components noted).

claim_text: The Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge opens as the world's longest sea-crossing.
notes: Oct 2018; ~55 km bridge-tunnel across the Pearl River estuary.

claim_text: Chang'e 4 makes the first-ever soft landing on the far side of the Moon.
source: Standard histories of the Chinese space program
notes: Jan 2019; a genuine world first in lunar exploration.

claim_text: China begins commercial 5G and builds the world's largest 5G network.
notes: 2019 onward; majority of the world's 5G base stations within a few years.

claim_text: China declares the elimination of extreme rural poverty, lifting the last counties above its poverty line.
source: PRC official records; World Bank commentary
notes: Declared 2020-2021; official and definition-dependent (China's rural line differs from World Bank thresholds), but corroborated as a very large reduction.

claim_text: Chang'e 5 returns lunar samples to Earth, the first sample return since 1976.
source: Standard histories of the Chinese space program
notes: Dec 2020; ~1.7 kg of lunar material.

claim_text: China completes the BeiDou-3 global satellite navigation system, an independent alternative to GPS.
notes: 2020; global positioning coverage.

claim_text: China's Tianwen-1 mission lands the Zhurong rover on Mars.
source: Standard histories of the Chinese space program
notes: May 2021; second nation to operate a rover on Mars.

claim_text: China completes the Tiangong space station in orbit.
source: Standard histories of the Chinese space program
notes: Core module 2021; three-module station completed 2022; a crewed national space station.

claim_text: China becomes the world's largest motor-vehicle exporter, led by electric vehicles.
notes: 2023; surpassed Japan; BYD and others drive an EV-led export surge.

claim_text: Chang'e 6 returns the first samples ever collected from the far side of the Moon.
source: Standard histories of the Chinese space program
notes: June 2024; another world first in lunar exploration.

claim_text: DeepSeek releases a competitive large language model at a fraction of typical training cost, jolting the global AI industry.
notes: Jan 2025; signaled China's fast-following capability in frontier AI at low cost.

claim_text: Huawei is founded in Shenzhen, later becoming the world's largest telecommunications-equipment maker and a 5G leader.
notes: Founding anchored to 1987; also a top global smartphone maker; later central to US-China tech tensions (part of the record). Added in the v0.2 country-blind recode as a previously-omitted innovation row.

claim_text: BYD is founded, later becoming the world's largest manufacturer of electric and new-energy vehicles.
notes: Founded 1995 as a battery maker; entered autos 2003; overtook Tesla in quarterly battery-EV sales in 2023. Added in the v0.2 recode as a previously-omitted innovation row.

claim_text: DJI is founded, later dominating the global consumer and commercial drone market.
notes: Founded 2006; grew to an estimated majority share of the world consumer-drone market. Added in the v0.2 recode as a previously-omitted innovation row.

claim_text: CATL is founded, later becoming the world's largest maker of electric-vehicle batteries.
notes: Founded 2011; world's largest EV-battery supplier by installed capacity within roughly a decade. Added in the v0.2 recode as a previously-omitted innovation row.

claim_text: ByteDance is founded, later creating Douyin/TikTok, the first Chinese consumer-internet platform to reach mass global scale.
notes: Founded 2012; TikTok launched internationally ~2017; AI-driven recommendation; subject to data and geopolitical disputes abroad (part of the record). Added in the v0.2 recode as a previously-omitted innovation row.
